name: Budesonide
drug_class: Glucocorticoid (inhaled, nasal and locally acting oral)
route_note: Inhaled for asthma/COPD; nasal spray; modified-release oral capsules/tablets or orodispersible tablets and rectal foam for gut disease

discovery.note: A non-halogenated glucocorticoid with high topical potency and extensive first-pass hepatic inactivation.

rx_status: prescription; nasal spray OTC in some countries
tagline: Topically potent corticosteroid for asthma, rhinitis, IBD and IgA nephropathy
summary: Budesonide is a glucocorticoid with strong local anti-inflammatory activity but about 85–90% first-pass liver metabolism, limiting systemic effects. It is a mainstay inhaled corticosteroid in asthma and COPD and is also formulated for rhinitis, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, eosinophilic oesophagitis and IgA nephropathy.
mechanism: Budesonide binds the cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptor; the complex moves to the nucleus, where it represses pro-inflammatory transcription factors such as NF-κB and AP-1 and induces anti-inflammatory genes.

The result is reduced airway eosinophilia, mucosal oedema and cytokine production. Inhaled or gut-targeted formulations deliver it where needed, and rapid CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver limits systemic exposure from the swallowed fraction.
uses: Maintenance treatment of asthma (alone or with formoterol)
Mild to moderate Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis

history.title: First marketed
history.detail: Introduced as an inhaled asthma treatment (Pulmicort).

history.title: Nebulised steroid
history.detail: Pulmicort Respules becomes the first nebulised corticosteroid approved in the US, for young children.

history.title: Crohn's disease
history.detail: FDA approves Entocort EC capsules for Crohn's disease.

history.title: Ulcerative colitis
history.detail: FDA approves Uceris extended-release tablets for ulcerative colitis.

history.title: Eosinophilic oesophagitis (EU)
history.detail: EMA approves Jorveza orodispersible tablets for eosinophilic oesophagitis.

history.title: IgA nephropathy
history.detail: FDA grants accelerated approval to Tarpeyo (Calliditas) to reduce proteinuria in IgA nephropathy.

history.title: Reliever combination
history.detail: FDA approves Airsupra (albuterol/budesonide) as an as-needed asthma inhaler.

history.title: Eohilia
history.detail: FDA approves Eohilia oral suspension, the first oral treatment for eosinophilic oesophagitis in the US.

pk.bioavailability: Oral ~10–15% (extensive first pass); inhaled ~ one third of nominal dose reaches circulation via lungs

serious: Cushingoid effects, particularly with CYP3A4 inhibitors

facts: Inhaled budesonide is one of the few inhaled corticosteroids with substantial pregnancy safety data.
In 2023 FDA approved Airsupra, pairing budesonide with albuterol in an as-needed reliever.
